summary.oneLiner: Gujarat Hotels Limited is a single-asset hospitality company that owns Welcomhotel Vadodara and licenses its operation to ITC Hotels Limited, earning license fee income of Rs 461.94 lakhs in FY2025-26.
summary.business: The Company owns a single upscale hotel property, Welcomhotel Vadodara, which it does not operate itself: the hotel is licensed to ITC Hotels Limited ('ITCHL') under an operating/licence arrangement, and the Company's income is principally the licence fee received from ITCHL. The hotel serves upscale room demand in Vadodara, Gujarat, and its Food & Beverage operations, described by the Board as a major strength, include the Peshawri restaurant and Welcomcafe Cambay. The Company has no subsidiary, associate or joint venture of its own.

risks.note: The Company's operations comprise one hotel, Welcomhotel Vadodara, which is licensed to ITC Hotels Limited; the Company's income is principally the licence fee from that one counterparty, and it has no subsidiary, associate or joint venture to diversify it. The receivable balances disclosed are with the Lessee under the Operating Service Agreement.

risks.risk: Leasehold land tenure not yet converted to freehold
risks.note: The hotel stands on leasehold land. The Company has filed a writ petition in the Gujarat High Court seeking a direction to the Gujarat State Government to act on its application for conversion to freehold and transfer to the Company; the matter remains unresolved (refer Note No. 20A).

Management states that after a strong start to the year, travel activity was impacted by geopolitical tensions, aviation-related disruptions, adverse weather events and the West Asian conflict, which resulted in deferment of travel decisions and softer travel momentum.

risks.risk: Inflation and energy prices weighing on discretionary consumption
risks.note: The West Asia conflict is described as a significant source of uncertainty since March 2026; the resultant supply-side disruption and elevated energy prices raise the risk of near-term inflationary pressures while also weighing on private consumption and investor sentiment — hotel demand is discretionary spend.

risks.risk: Rising branded room supply in a market with weak local volume growth
risks.note: Branded hotel room supply expanded 7.8% Y-o-Y with nearly 41% of new 2025 supply in the premium (upscale and above) segment and most of it added outside the top ten markets. In the Company's own market, upscale room demand in Gujarat grew only 6% and Vadodara city just 2%, making the market rate-led (Vadodara RevPAR +14%) rather than volume-led.

risks.risk: Market price and interest-rate risk on treasury investments
risks.note: The Company's surplus is deployed in mutual fund schemes, which the notes state are susceptible to market price risk arising mainly from changes in interest rates, which may impact the return and value of such investments.

risks.risk: Inherent limitations of the internal control framework
risks.note: The Board explicitly recognises that any internal financial control framework, however well designed, has inherent limitations, and relies on regular audit and review processes (internal audits by M/s Shah & Talati, Chartered Accountants, reviewed by the Audit Committee) to reinforce it.

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- The Company's operations comprise one hotel, Welcomhotel Vadodara, which is licensed to ITC Hotels Limited; the Company's income is principally the licence fee from that one counterparty, and it has no subsidiary, associate or joint venture to diversify it. The receivable balances disclosed are with the Lessee under the Operating Service Agreement.
- The hotel stands on leasehold land. The Company has filed a writ petition in the Gujarat High Court seeking a direction to the Gujarat State Government to act on its application for conversion to freehold and transfer to the Company; the matter remains unresolved (refer Note No. 20A).
- Management states that after a strong start to the year, travel activity was impacted by geopolitical tensions, aviation-related disruptions, adverse weather events and the West Asian conflict, which resulted in deferment of travel decisions and softer travel momentum.
- The West Asia conflict is described as a significant source of uncertainty since March 2026; the resultant supply-side disruption and elevated energy prices raise the risk of near-term inflationary pressures while also weighing on private consumption and investor sentiment — hotel demand is discretionary spend.
- Branded hotel room supply expanded 7.8% Y-o-Y with nearly 41% of new 2025 supply in the premium (upscale and above) segment and most of it added outside the top ten markets. In the Company's own market, upscale room demand in Gujarat grew only 6% and Vadodara city just 2%, making the market rate-led (Vadodara RevPAR +14%) rather than volume-led.
- The Company's surplus is deployed in mutual fund schemes, which the notes state are susceptible to market price risk arising mainly from changes in interest rates, which may impact the return and value of such investments.
- The Board explicitly recognises that any internal financial control framework, however well designed, has inherent limitations, and relies on regular audit and review processes (internal audits by M/s Shah & Talati, Chartered Accountants, reviewed by the Audit Committee) to reinforce it.
